messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity - GPU runtime errors observed across inference fleet (node flaps + container restarts). Root signal: repeated CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS on several A100 nodes. Pager: @Mike Chen oncall.

Mike Chen: seeing spikes in 502/500 and OOMs shortly after model load. logs attached from node gpu-a-12:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] E inference: runtime: failed step: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (cuLaunchKernel)
stack: runtime.cu:0x4f2a, loader.cu:0x15c, launch.cu:0x09b
Killed process 31457 (python) due to signal 9
```

Sanjay Patel: copying dmesg from same host — kernel messages show address translation faults right before the crash:
```
Mar 15 08:11:58 gpu-a-12 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has a pending address fault.
Mar 15 08:12:00 gpu-a-12 kernel: nvidia: illegal memory access at 0x7fffd3c20000, pid=31457
Mar 15 08:12:02 gpu-a-12 kernel: rmmod: attempt to remove unknown module nvidia_drm
```

Katie W: short summary for customers: some inference requests returned errors or timed out for models running on the affected A100 pool. Early estimate: ~4% of requests for redwood-7b-quant in region-us-west-2 between 08:10-08:20 impacted. We're triaging.

Devon R: action plan (immediate):
- cordon node gpu-a-12 and drain non-critical pods
- restart nvidia-persistenced + container runtime on drained nodes
- fallback routing: shift new traffic off A100 pool to mixed-gpu and cpu-fallback pool for critical customers (canary 3 nodes)
- temporarily disable prefetching in runtime for in-flight loads (env var RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0)

Anna Morales: started customer comms for top 10 affected accounts. Notifying enterprise customers and opening support tickets.

ops-bot: @channel Automated mitigation started: cordon gpu-a-12, draining 4 pods.

Mike Chen: running `kubectl drain gpu-a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` now. Observed immediate crash in one of the draining pods that triggered OOM and container restart loop; attaching container logs:
```
E tensor: kv_cache_resize failed: oob write at offset 0x1fffe000 (len 4096)
E runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at tensor.cu:0x22f
```

Sanjay Patel: hypothesis: kernel-level race on memory mapping or a driver bug triggered by a particular sequence of allocations during model kv-cache growth. Could be aggravated by recent driver update (nvidia-driver 525.85 -> 525.91 rolled yesterday).

Katie W: ask: do we have a safe rollback plan? If driver is implicated we should roll back to 525.85 on a small canary set and watch. Also consider pinning model to smaller kv-cache config to avoid growth pattern.

Devon R: rolling back drivers is heavy. Immediate safer mitigations:
- use runtime fallback to quantized CPU variant for new sessions for customers with high error rates
- set RUNTIME_MAX_KV=1024 for redwood-7b-quant on A100 pool (limits growth)
- disable async allocation path: export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 in runtime to make allocation failures deterministic while we triage

Anna Morales: Customers updated: "We're routing your traffic to alternate capacity; some requests may see slightly higher latency. We're investigating root cause and will update in 1 hour." Response from acme-inc: "We need an ETA for full recovery; some batches failed in production."

Mike Chen: checklist updates: x-ing off cordon/drain, restarting nvidia-persistenced on 3 nodes. Next: snapshot /var/log/nvidia* + kernel logs for nodes that crashed; will upload to incident ticket #INC-14532.

Sanjay Patel: collecting core dumps now. Please do not reboot affected nodes until we've pulled `/var/crash/*.core` and `nv_stack_report.txt`. Also capture `nvidia-smi -q -x` and `dmesg -T` outputs.

ops-bot: NOTICE: Canary traffic shifted: 5% -> mixed-gpu pool, 95% -> cpu-fallback for impacted customers.

Devon R: quick experiment: we booted a small canary with driver 525.85 and reloaded model; no immediate illegal-address errors after 12 minutes. Not conclusive but suggestive.

Mike Chen: plan for next 2 hours:
- continue draining remaining suspect nodes (done: gpu-a-12, gpu-a-14)
- schedule controlled rollback of driver on two more nodes as test
- full continuity: keep fallback routing in place until rollback proves stable or kernel vendor confirms fix
- assign postmortem owner: @Sanjay Patel

Anna Morales: tagging legal & compliance due to enterprise SLA impact. Also creating dedicated status page entry.

Katie W: note to oncall: collect p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and request counts for affected model and customers between 08:00-09:30. Save metrics to incident ticket.

Sanjay Patel: follow-up: captured kdump and forwarded to driver vendor with logs. Created internal bug: INF-4321 (title: "A100 - boundary violation during KV cache growth -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS").

Mike Chen: thanks all. If anyone sees repeat crashes after rollback tests, ping me and escalate to kernel team. We'll reconvene in 30m. :thumbsup:"
